value_source: Services Australia, AIR vaccine code formats (Standard vaccines and Non-standard vaccines tables)
rationale: Services Australia publishes the complete AIR vaccine code list that software products must use to submit AIR episodes, and the published column heading 'Vaccine/Brand Name, Vaccine Code' matches this field's description 'Vaccine/Product code' exactly; I read 95 standard and 70 non-standard codes off the page (165 in total) and sampled 35 here.
evidence_quote: Vaccine/Brand Name Vaccine Code: Comirnaty COMIRN; Infanrix hexa IFHX; Prevenar 13 PRVTH
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review said the AIR vaccine-product codeframe was unpublished. It is published, by Services Australia, as the AIR vaccine code formats page for software vendors.

value_domain: Sequence number: positive integer counter within an individual (inferred)
rationale: The official description calls it 'the unique contraindication sequence number', so the domain is an integer counter that increments per contraindication record, not a codeframe; the sibling fields ENCSEQ, CLAIMSEQ and VACCSEQ in the same AIR extract use the same sequence-number pattern.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review grouped this with the unpublished AIR codeframes. A sequence number has no codeframe to publish; its domain follows from the description and does not need one.

value_domain: Timestamp: date and time the contraindication record was written (inferred)
rationale: The description is 'Contraindication timestamp' and the _TSP suffix is the standard timestamp suffix in this extract, so the domain is a datetime within the collection's 2010-to-current window, bracketed by the CONTRSDT and CONTREDT contraindication start and end dates in the same table.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review treated this as an unpublished codeframe. It is a timestamp; there is no codeframe to publish and the domain follows from the type.

value_domain: Medicare provider number: 6-digit stem, 1 alphanumeric location character, 1 alpha check character (inferred)
value_source: AIHW METeOR, Medicare provider stem number (identifier format)
rationale: The description is 'Checked provider number supplying the contra-indication information', and AIR contraindications can only be certified by a health professional using their Medicare provider number, so the domain is the published 8-character Medicare provider number format rather than a codeframe; the sibling fields CPROVNUM, CIMMPROV and PROVNUM in the same extract are the same kind of field and are already treated as supported.
evidence_quote: denotes the practice location, followed by an alpha character which is a check character
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review lumped this with unpublished codeframes. A provider number is an identifier with a published format, not a codeframe, and the AIR extract's other provider-number fields are already handled.

value_domain: Medicare provider number: 6-digit stem, 1 alphanumeric location character, 1 alpha check character (inferred)
value_source: AIHW METeOR, Medicare provider stem number (identifier format)
rationale: The description is 'Checked provider number reporting the most recent Individual conscientious objection', so the value is a Medicare provider number in the published 8-character format, not a code from a classification; the conscientious-objection content is sensitive but the provider number's shape is not.
evidence_quote: denotes the practice location, followed by an alpha character which is a check character
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review treated this as an unpublished codeframe. It is a provider identifier with a published format; the sensitivity of the surrounding conscientious-objection fields does not make the identifier's shape unknowable.

value_domain: AIR vaccination provider type (inferred; internal code values not published)
values: Aboriginal Health Service or Aboriginal Medical Service (AMS)
Community health centre or community health service
value_source: Services Australia, Provider types who can register as a vaccination provider
rationale: Services Australia publishes the closed list of provider types an organisation must select when registering for an AIR provider number, and this field is the 'Provider practice type code' on the AIR provider record, so the categories are the published ones; the page names the 13 categories but publishes no code values, so the codes themselves are inferred one-to-one from the categories.
evidence_quote: Aboriginal Health Service or Aboriginal Medical Service (AMS), Authorised Nurse Immuniser (ANI), Commercial provider, Council
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review found no published provider codeframe and stopped there. The categories are published even though the codes are not, which is enough for a defensible guessed domain.

value_domain: Grouping of AIR vaccination provider types (inferred; grouping rule and code values not published)
values: Aboriginal Health Service or Aboriginal Medical Service (AMS)
Community health centre or community health service
value_source: Services Australia, Provider types who can register as a vaccination provider
rationale: The description, 'Provider categorisation derived from provider information', points at a rollup of the AIR provider practice type, so the underlying categories are the published Services Australia provider types; the _GRP suffix says a coarser grouping is applied, and neither that grouping rule nor its codes are published, so the domain is at best the ungrouped list.
evidence_quote: Aboriginal Health Service or Aboriginal Medical Service (AMS), Authorised Nurse Immuniser (ANI), Commercial provider, Council
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review found no published codeframe. The underlying categories are published; only the rollup is not, so a coarse domain is defensible.

values: Aboriginal Health Service or Aboriginal Medical Service (AMS)

evidence_quote: Aboriginal Health Service or Aboriginal Medical Service (AMS), Council, Pharmacy, Private hospital, Public hospital

value_domain: Record type code identifying the AIR extract record layout; short alphanumeric, effectively constant within each table (inferred)
rationale: The description, 'The type of information sent in the file', plus the field's presence on all five AIR extract tables (childloc, contrind, episode, provider, vaccstat) says it is the record-type marker of a fixed-format transfer file, which tells the reader which layout to parse; the value is therefore a short code that is constant within each PLIDA table, and the code values are not published.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review treated this as an unpublished codeframe. It is a file-format record marker, and its shape (a short code, one per record layout) follows from the description and from the field appearing once on every table.

value_domain: School identifier: numeric school code (inferred; issuing authority not established)
value_source: ACARA Data Catalogue (School ID format, as the national candidate identifier)
rationale: The field is an identifier, not a classification: it records which school a school-based immunisation episode was delivered at, so its domain is a school code drawn from a register rather than a codeframe. I checked whether the ACARA school ID applies and found no AIR or Services Australia documentation naming it; ACARA's own catalogue gives the national format, but state and territory school immunisation programmes may report jurisdiction school codes instead.
evidence_quote: School ID: School code, left zero-padded to 9 digits.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review lumped an identifier in with codeframes. An identifier needs a format, not a code list, and a numeric school code is defensible even though the issuing register is unconfirmed.

value_domain: Short reason code from a small closed set, explaining the episode status (inferred; code values not published)
rationale: The field sits directly beside EPSSTAT, 'Episode status code', in the AIR episode table, which is the standard status-and-reason pairing of a transaction register: the reason code says why the episode carries its current status. The AIR message specifications that would list the values sit behind Services Australia's licensed Health Systems Developer Portal and are not public, so the shape is defensible but the values are not.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review was right that the values are unpublished, but the shape - a short code from a small closed set paired with EPSSTAT - is defensible and better than typed missing.

value_domain: Short reason code from a small closed set, explaining why the individual's AIR record ended (inferred; code values not published)
rationale: The field pairs with EDT, 'Individual end date', in the childloc table, so it records why a record closed on that date; the domain is a short code from a small closed set. The AIR message specifications that would name the values are behind Services Australia's licensed developer portal, so I will not assert labels.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review was right that the values are unpublished, but the shape - a short reason code paired with the end date - is defensible and better than typed missing.

value_domain: Yes/No indicator (inferred from the _IND naming convention; the meaning of DEC is not established)
rationale: Every other _IND field in ndis_participantdemographics is a binary flag - ACTVPRTCPNTIND, AUSTCTZNIND, CMPNSTNIND, CSNIND, CURRYPIRACIND, EVERELIGBLIND, EVERYPIRACIND, INJURYIND, RACIND - and the package already reads SSA_IND and CHC_FLAG as Y/N, so the suffix fixes the domain even though it does not fix the meaning; the presence of DEATHDT in the same table makes 'deceased indicator' the likeliest reading, but the Y/N domain holds under any of the candidate readings.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review declined because the name did not distinguish a deceased flag from a decision or declaration flag. That question does not need answering: all the candidate readings are binary indicators, so the domain is fixed by the naming convention alone.

value_domain: Yes/No indicator: participant has a recorded goal to leave residential aged care (inferred)
value_source: NDIA quarterly reporting on younger people in residential aged care (supports the concept, not the code values)
rationale: The _IND suffix fixes a binary domain on the same convention as the other flags in this table, and the field sits in a block of younger-people-in-residential-aged-care fields (RACIND, CURRYPIRACIND, EVERYPIRACIND), where 'has a goal to leave residential aged care' is a measure the NDIA reports quarterly - 475 of 1,433 participants under 65 living in residential aged care as at 31 December 2023.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review said no public NDIS goal data rule defines the indicator. That is true of the code values but not of the shape: the _IND convention and the surrounding YPIRAC fields make a Y/N flag defensible.

value_domain: Yes/No indicator: participant has housing support after residential aged care (inferred; low confidence)
rationale: Read against the table's abbreviation conventions the name expands to 'post RAC housing support', and RAC means residential aged care elsewhere in this table (RACIND, CURRYPIRACIND); it sits in the same YPIRAC block as GOALTOLEAVEIND, where the NDIA's companion measure is whether a participant has housing supports funded in their plan, which is binary. I flag the risk plainly: the field carries none of the table's type suffixes (_IND, _CD, _NM, _DT), so it could instead be a short text field naming a home-and-living support type such as SDA, SIL or ILO, and I cannot rule that out.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review said the abbreviated name could not fix a support, status or indicator domain. The YPIRAC context around it narrows the reading enough for a low-confidence binary guess, though the reviewer's caution was reasonable.

value_domain: Modified Monash Model category, MM1 to MM7 (inferred)
value_source: Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, Modified Monash Model classifications table
rationale: I favour the MMM reading over the Data Item List's 'Meshblock code' description. The name decomposes on this table's own convention - RSDSIN means 'resides in', as in RSDSINSTATECD and RSDSINSRVCDSTRCTNM, and CD means code - giving 'resides in MMM code'; it pairs naturally with NDISMMMSCD, the NDIS-adjusted MMM, as the unadjusted MMM of the participant's address. An 11-digit mesh block would also be far more identifying than anything else released at participant level in this table, whereas MMM is a seven-category variable. The published labels are written MM 1 to MM 7; whether the field stores 1-7 or MM1-MM7 is not established.
evidence_quote: MM 1 Metropolitan areas: Major cities accounting for 70% of Australia's population.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review declined because no crosswalk resolved the name-versus-description conflict. A crosswalk is not what resolves it: the table's own abbreviation convention and its sibling NDISMMMSCD do, and the disclosure argument runs the same way.

value_domain: Commonwealth Home Support Programme service type, pre-1 July 2025 service list (inferred; internal code values not published)
value_source: Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, CHSP Service List Mapping Guide (June 2025), Appendix A: old service list pre-1 July 2025
rationale: The field only appears on chsp_episode tables, so it is the Commonwealth Home Support Programme service type, not a general aged care programme type, and the tables cover 2016 to current so the pre-1 July 2025 CHSP service list applies. The Department's mapping guide publishes that list under the three-level Service / Service type / Service sub-type structure that also explains the companion fields SERVICE_TYPE_DESC and SERVICE_SUBTYPE_DESC. I read all 17 old service types off Appendix A; the guide publishes the categories but no code values, so the codes must be synthesised one-to-one with these labels. Sector support and development is excluded because it is a provider-level activity rather than a client service.
evidence_quote: Old Service type: Allied health and therapy services ... Domestic assistance ... Specialised support services
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review said the NACDC service descriptors do not establish the internal code values, which is correct, but the classification behind them is published in full by the Department, so the categories are defensible even where the codes are not.
